structure:
A Playwright trace corpus from the tests repo (trade-imports-ins-tests) run against the workspace stack built from latest main: workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/traces-e2e/ holds one folder per test result, each with a trace.zip, plus report.json (the Playwright JSON report), which is the index: it maps every test to its spec file, line, describe block, project and trace folder. 191 results from 68 spec files: 178 in the animals project (tests/animals/e2e: 36 feature specs incl. 7 under features/address-book, 4 journey specs incl. 3 under journeys/persistence, 17 page specs, 1 visual spec) and 13 in the ins project (tests/ins/e2e/features: 7 address-book specs and 3 others). 183 passed first time, 6 were skipped (the five per-role 'offers no INS add link in stub mode' tests in addresses-read-only.spec.ts and 'offers no way to add an address in stub mode' in contact-address.spec.ts, all skipped because the full stack was running, yet each left a trace), and 2 timed out on the first attempt then passed on retry (notification-dashboard.spec.ts 'copies a submitted notification from its searched dashboard card' and transited-countries.spec.ts 'transit countries are optional: continuing with none saves and goes on'): both attempts have their own folder (the retry's ends -retry1). No test failed. Most traces are UI walks with DOM frame-snapshots (a page-control trace runs to about 30 actions and 60 snapshots); a few lifecycle and persistence traces are mainly API requests with few or no snapshots. Reading the traces: tim distil trace runs Playwright 1.62.1, and these traces were recorded by Playwright 1.64 (alpha), so 'open' refuses them with TraceVersionError. Each part agent unzips each trace.zip into its own part folder under distil/extract/trace-e2e.work/ and reads the N-trace.trace files (before/after actions, frame-snapshot DOM, log), N-trace.network (requests and responses) and test.trace (test steps and assertions) with jq; try 'tim distil trace ... -- open' first in case the viewer has been upgraded. The spec files under repos/trade-imports-ins-tests/tests/ name what each test asserts; the checkout may have moved on since the run, so where a spec and its trace disagree the trace wins. Cut: by spec file, grouped along the journey into 15 parts of 8 to 16 traces each: sign-in and headers, dashboard search and sort, the dashboard page and delete, the journey pages in order (origin and reason, commodities and consignment, identification and CPH, contact address, copied addresses, the picker and INS handshake, arrival and transit, transporters, documents), the hub, check your answers and view states, the lifecycle and persistence, and the ins project. Scope leaves out nothing in the folder: every result in report.json is in exactly one part. Being a trace corpus it is a lower bound: a page, branch or error no test walked is not in it.

Extracted in 15 parts:
Part 1, Sign-in, sign-out and security headers (animals): Part 1 mined all 11 trace zips named in its read (10 from tests/animals/e2e/features/auth.spec.ts, 1 from tests/animals/e2e/features/headers.spec.ts) and read both spec files in full. Every trace passed. The tim distil trace CLI refused to open these zips (TraceVersionError: the traces were written by a newer Playwright than the viewer tim installs), so each zip, already unzipped under the part's working folder as <hash>/, was mined directly: the browser actions from <hash>/1-trace.trace (type=before events), the DOM from its frame-snapshots (rendered to <hash>.html with render.jq), and the network log from <hash>/1-trace.network (resource-snapshots: method, status, URL, Location, Set-Cookie, Content-Security-Policy). Refs below use 'trace <hash> action call@<n>' for actions and DOM, and 'trace <hash> request <method> <path>' for the network log. Pages reached, in order: (1) the animals frontend dashboard URL /live-animals, which unauthenticated returns 302 to /auth/sign-in?redirect=<path>, which returns 302 to the Defra ID stub authorise endpoint on localhost:3007, which returns 302 to (2) the stub sign-in page 'Sign in using Government Gateway' at /dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp; a bad user id or bad password re-renders that page with status 400 and an error summary; a good one returns 302 to the stub /organisations, which returns 302 straight back to the frontend /auth/sign-in-oidc with a code, which returns 302 to the stored redirect path: (3) the dashboard 'Import notification service' (heading, header navigation and Log out link only; the dashboard body belongs to parts 2 and 3) or (4) a deep journey page, 'Origin of the import', for an existing draft. Log out goes /auth/sign-out, 302 to the stub end-session URL, which renders (5) the stub page 'You have signed out'. The service root / returns 302 to /live-animals. The headers trace reloads the dashboard and records the Content-Security-Policy and other security headers on the document response. Always-present pages: sign-in, dashboard. Conditional: the error state of the sign-in page (bad credentials), the signed-out page (after Log out), the deep-link return (only when a deep link started the sign-in). Platform chrome (skip link, GOV.UK header, footer, phase banners) is left out except where it carries the sign-out control or the signed-in identity. Surfaces the slice should show and does not (empty submissions, session expiry, the post-logout callback, organisation choice, the unauthenticated root) are recorded as gaps.
Part 2, Dashboard search and sort (animals): Part 2, Dashboard search and sort (animals). Read both specs in full (tests/animals/e2e/features/notification-dashboard-search.spec.ts, 7 tests; notification-dashboard-sort.spec.ts, 6 tests) and mined all 13 trace zips the part names, none sampled: c7374 (search form shown), 12d83 (complete reference returns one match), 861a9 (View after search opens notification view), b4432 (no matches), 0b7b1 (free text), c23e0 (sort after search keeps reference), 4da5f (page param keeps reference), 00377 (default sort), 6c8f9 (four sort options), 3fd8a / 6f16e / 73232 / fc4b8 (submit each sort option). The trace CLI that tim installs refuses these zips (TraceVersionError: the traces were recorded by a newer Playwright), so each zip was unpacked into the part's working folder (t01..t13, in read order, matched to its test by its recorded actions and query strings) and read directly: the test.trace step log (every Navigate, Fill, Click, Select option and Expect, with locators and values), the browser-context network log, and the frame snapshots of the dashboard rendered to HTML. One page is in scope, the live-animals dashboard at /live-animals (caption 'Dashboard', H1 'Import notification service', H2 'Your notifications'). Its left third is an aside headed 'Filter notifications' holding a GET search form (hidden sort, 'Keyword or reference' text input, 'Search' button); its right two thirds open with a toolbar holding the results label and a GET sort form ('Sort by' select with four options, hidden referenceNumber when a search is active, 'Update sort' secondary button). States seen: unfiltered (Showing 1 to 25 of N Results), one match (Showing 1 Result), no match and free text (No notifications found, no cards, no pagination, no error summary), each of the four sorts selected, and a referenceNumber plus page=2 URL. One page outside the slice is reached: the notification view ('Review your notification') via a card's View link. Cards, their actions, pagination and delete belong to part 3 and are claimed here only where they carry the search or sort state in a URL. Everything is server-rendered: the browser made only full-page GETs to /live-animals, so the search and sort calls behind the page never appear in the traces.
Part 3, Dashboard page, cards, pagination and delete (animals): Part 3 mined all 12 trace zips its read names, from three spec files in the tests repo's animals project: features/notification-delete.spec.ts (2: deletes a draft notification [9d8f3]; deletes the notification and removes it from the dashboard [2e3c2]), pages/notification-dashboard-pagination.spec.ts (1: uses GOV.UK pagination and reports the result range [029ca]) and pages/notification-dashboard.spec.ts (9: starts a journey at the origin page and lists the draft [93765]; lands on the notification dashboard [c058e]; allows creating a new notification, landing on the journey entry page [7d727]; displays the notification list and result count [2ad56]; displays details on a notification card [118d4]; shows resume, copy and delete actions for a draft notification [015ef]; shows view, copy and amend actions for a submitted notification [e7a9a]; copies a submitted notification from its searched dashboard card, first attempt timed out [a1f4f] and retry 1 passed [a1f4f-retry1]). The bundled trace viewer refused every zip (TraceVersionError: recorded by Playwright 1.64 alpha), so each zip was unzipped into this part's work folder and read with jq: N-trace.trace (before/after actions, frame-snapshot DOM rendered back to HTML from the snapshot arrays), N-trace.network (resource snapshots) and test.trace (steps and errors); the failed attempt's final screen came from its last screencast frame. Refs below name the trace by its folder hash fragment, then the call id and snapshot phase. Pages in this slice, in the order a user meets them: (1) the animals dashboard at /live-animals (caption Dashboard, h1 Import notification service, Start a new notification start button, Your notifications, a Filter notifications aside with the Keyword or reference search, a toolbar with the result count and Sort by, then up to 25 GOV.UK summary cards and GOV.UK block pagination); its variants are unfiltered (Showing 1 to 25 of N Results with Next), page 2 (?page=2, Showing 26 to 50 of N Results, Previous and Next), searched to one card (Showing 1 Result), searched to none (No notifications found) and after a delete (?deleted=1, success notification banner); (2) the notification card itself, whose action list depends on status: Draft (blue tag) offers Resume, Copy as new, Delete; Submitted (green) offers View, Amend, Copy as new, Delete; Amending (yellow, seen in the list but not driven) offers Resume, Copy as new, Cancel amendment, Delete; (3) the delete confirmation at /live-animals/notifications/{ref}/delete (Delete this notification?), reached by direct URL for a draft and from the card's Delete link for a submitted notification; (4) the journey entry page the Start button lands on, /notifications/{ref}/origin (Origin of the import), mined only for what proves the landing, since its fields belong to the origin part; (5) the overview at /notifications/{ref} (Overview), reached by Resume and by Copy as new, mined only for the reference strip and, after a copy, what the new draft carries. The copy test's first attempt never reached the dashboard: it timed out after 90 s in the UI submit journey when the place-of-destination picker search returned HTTP 500 and rendered a bare 500 error page. Network logs show only browser-to-frontend traffic; seeding runs through the frontend's own form posts from an API request context, plus address-book lookups. What is conditional: the card actions (by status), the pagination links (by page and total), the result-count wording (by result count) and the success banner (by ?deleted=1).
Part 4, Origin, port of entry and reason for import (animals journey): Part 4 mined 16 trace zips from six spec files of the tests repo's animals project (all passed): features/country-of-origin-type-ahead.spec.ts (1), features/port-of-entry-select.spec.ts (1), features/reason-purpose-scope.spec.ts (1), pages/import-reason.spec.ts (5), pages/origin.spec.ts (7) and visual/origin-of-import.visual.spec.ts (1). All six spec files were read in full. The zips were written by a newer Playwright than the trace CLI tim installs (TraceVersionError on open), so each zip was read from its unpacked event files with jq: every action (before events), every network request (resource snapshots) and every full DOM snapshot of <main> and the page title and back link; the visual trace's screencast frame was viewed. Short names used in refs: T01 = animals-e2e-features-count-09462-ountry-code-and-persists-it-animals, T02 = animals-e2e-features-port--60da8-bmits-and-persists-the-code-animals, T03 = animals-e2e-features-reaso-187a4-ped-when-the-reason-changes-animals, T04 = animals-e2e-pages-import-r-bf303-e-renders-the-page-controls-animals, T05 = animals-e2e-pages-import-r-1dcd8-rt-reason-unchecked-on-load-animals, T06 = animals-e2e-pages-import-r-3f715-cepts-a-valid-import-reason-animals, T07 = animals-e2e-pages-import-r-1907f-arket-reason-and-accepts-it-animals, T08 = animals-e2e-pages-import-r-39ca5--the-internal-market-reason-animals, T09 = animals-e2e-pages-origin-O-bc0fa-e-renders-the-page-controls-animals, T10 = animals-e2e-pages-origin-O-556ac-he-country-selector-on-load-animals, T11 = animals-e2e-pages-origin-O-0d4b9-ccepts-valid-origin-details-animals, T12 = animals-e2e-pages-origin-O-44f41-submitted-without-a-country-animals, T13 = animals-e2e-pages-origin-O-9e670-de-is-claimed-but-not-given-animals, T14 = animals-e2e-pages-origin-O-5cbc4-on-of-origin-code-selection-animals, T15 = animals-e2e-pages-origin-O-d8fed-untry-subdivision-selection-animals, T16 = animals-e2e-visual-origin--55e4a-ge-appearance-on-first-load-animals. Page inventory in journey order: (1) Origin of the import, /live-animals/notifications/{ref}/origin, always the first page after Start a new notification on the dashboard, and re-entered from the overview task 'Where is this consignment coming from?' (pointers T01 call@288 first load, T13 call@1315 error state, T14 call@1161 and T15 call@1092 return visits, T12 call@1080 return visit with no country); (2) Main reason for import, /import-reason, reached from the overview task 'Main reason for import', with conditional reveals per reason (pointers T03 call@704 first load, call@720 and call@738 return visits, call@744 and T08 call@1082 error state); (3) Arrival details, /port-of-entry, reached from the overview task 'Arrival details', of which only the Port of entry type-ahead is in this slice (pointers T02 call@629, call@637 list open, call@659 return visit). Pages the traces pass through on the way (dashboard, commodity search, commodity details, overview, additional details, transporter details) appear only as navigation targets here and belong to other parts. Every trace except T16 and T09/T10 crosses the origin page through the shared start-notification setup (France, No, Save and continue).
Part 5, Commodities, consignment details and additional details (animals journey): Part 5 mined all 14 trace zips its partition names, from four specs in the tests repo (all read in full): commodities.spec.ts (7 traces: 23432 search box and empty state, 7c5a8 query shorter than three characters, 2d57c grouping by commodity heading, a6ed6 no match, 66568 multiple pairs persisted across queries, 290a2 count and clear, 725f7 empty-submit error), consignment-details.spec.ts (3 traces: ca7de page controls, d0e23 number of animals empty on load, 0e33b valid save), additional-details.spec.ts (3 traces: af002 page controls, 7bbef unchecked on load, 6c9ed valid save) and features/additional-details-scope.spec.ts (1 trace: 1c358 unweaned-animals scope). Trace hashes in refs are the five-character hash in each trace folder name (for example animals-e2e-pages-commodit-66568-...). The tim-run Playwright trace CLI refused every zip (TraceVersionError: the trace was written by a newer Playwright than the viewer), so each zip, already unzipped in this part's working folder, was read directly with jq: the test.trace step log for actions (pw:api@N / expect@N ids), the N-trace.trace frame snapshots for rendered DOM (snapshot call@N ids), and the N-trace.network resource snapshots for the request log. Every trace's setup walks dashboard -> Start a new notification -> Origin of the import (France, No) -> overview; those pages belong to other parts and are claimed here only where they hand over to this slice. Page inventory, in journey order: (1) commodity selection, /live-animals/notifications/{ref}/commodities, H1 'What are you importing?', reached from the overview task 'What are you importing?' and from 'Add another commodity'; states seen: empty, short query, results, no match, selection panel, error summary. (2) commodity details, /consignment-details, H1 'Commodity details', always follows a successful commodity selection save; one section per commodity line, newest first. (3) additional details, /additional-details, H1 'Additional details', reached from the overview task 'Main reason for import' after the import-reason page saves; its unweaned-animals question is conditional on a triggering commodity line (seen with Bos taurus, absent with only Felis catus). Each page posts to itself and redirects (search re-renders with 200; saves 302 to the next page or the overview). No validation error was rendered on the commodity details or additional details pages in any trace; those error states, the Remove action, Save and return to overview, and the commodity-search back-end call are recorded as gaps.
Part 6, Animal identification and CPH number (animals journey): Part 6, Animal identification and CPH number (animals journey). Read the five spec files in full (pages/animal-identification.spec.ts, features/animal-identifiers-cap.spec.ts, features/animal-identifiers-conditional.spec.ts, pages/cph-number.spec.ts, features/cph-scope.spec.ts) and mined all 12 trace zips the part names, none sampled. The trace CLI run through tim distil trace still refuses every zip (TraceVersionError: recorded by a newer Playwright than the viewer tim installs; re-tried on 1654a for this run), so each zip is unzipped into trace-e2e.work/part6/<hash>/ and read raw: test.trace for the action list (every action transcribed), 1-trace.trace frame snapshots rendered to HTML (<hash>.main.html: main element and back link) for the rendered DOM, and 1-trace.network for the request log. The zips are unchanged since they were first unzipped (written 18:42, unzipped 20:27 the same day), so the unzipped files and renders in the part folder are this part's reading. Refs cite the trace by its folder hash and the snapshot callId (call@N) or test action id (pw:api@N / expect@N). Traces: f63b4 (cap: cattle, count 2, counter 1 of 2 -> 2 of 2 -> maximum reached, count-drop error on Commodity details, remove, count 1 saves), 34a64 (cats: identifier types plus permanent address, partial-address error then a committed record), c709d (cattle plus Atlantic salmon: card only for cattle), f123d (salmon only: identification page redirects to the overview), cf344 (CPH scope: cats -> no CPH row and Continue goes to overview; cattle added -> CPH row 'Not added yet', Add -> CPH page -> back to hub with 123456789, Change prefilled, Back to hub, Continue -> CPH page prefilled), 714ef / 80f8e / dc773 (identification page, cattle count 1: controls, empty ear tag, valid ear tag saves to overview), 1654a / b3987 / 2feb0 / a698a (CPH page reached sequentially from the addresses hub after all five parties added: controls, empty on load, valid 12/345/6789 saves to overview, empty submit gives 'Enter a CPH number' with HTTP 400). Pages in this slice, in journey order: Overview task row 'Identification details' (section '2. Description of the goods', conditional on an identifier-bearing commodity) -> Identification details (/commodities/identification: journey strip, caption, inset text, Selected commodities table, one card per identifier-bearing commodity line with its N-of-M unit form, saved-records table, Save and add another / Save and finish, maximum-reached state; page buttons Save and continue, Save and return to overview, Cancel and return to overview) -> Overview. Commodity details (/consignment-details) carries the count-drop error. Consignment addresses hub (/addresses) carries the CPH row only when a CPH-triggering commodity exists -> Add the county parish holding number (CPH) (/cph-number, or /cph-number?return=addresses from the hub row) -> Overview (sequential) or the hub (return=addresses). Conditional: the identification page and its task row exist only when a commodity line has an identifier type; the identifier fields per card depend on the commodity; the permanent address only for cats (dogs per the test title, not walked); the CPH row and the sequential CPH step exist only when a CPH-triggering line (cattle observed) exists. Only Bos taurus, Felis catus and Salmo salar were walked; dogs, horses and other species were not, and no identifier or CPH format validation was driven: each is a gap claim. The claims carry forward the earlier extract of this slice (ids trace-e2e-p6-001 to -102, all of which its verifier upheld) and add as -103 to -109 the facts that verifier found missing, each re-checked against the same traces.
Part 7, Contact address page and all six operators (animals journey): Part 7 mined all 8 trace zips its read names, from two spec files in the tests repo's animals project, and read both specs. pages/contact-address.spec.ts (7): renders the page controls [5b1a7]; leaves the contact address unchecked on load [943a0]; accepts a valid contact address [60f4b]; a chosen contact address is shown as the current contact on return, still chosen, and saving again keeps it [2fe1e]; saving with no contact address selected is allowed and exits to the hub [2cb78]; offers no way to add an address in stub mode [676b1, skipped: its test.trace carries the skip annotation and ends after the beforeEach walk, so it shows the page as rendered outside stub mode]; links to INS to add an address when the full stack is running [b077b]. features/all-operators.spec.ts (1): check your answers lists all six operators with the picked name and country [5c7f8]. The bundled trace viewer refuses these zips (TraceVersionError: recorded by a newer Playwright), so each zip, already unzipped into this part's work folder, was read with jq: 1-trace.trace (before events for the action list, frame snapshots rendered back to HTML), 1-trace.network (resource snapshots with post params) and test.trace (steps and annotations). Refs name the trace by its folder hash fragment, then the call id. Pages in this slice, in the order a user meets them: (1) the Overview at /live-animals/notifications/{ref}, mined only for the '6. Contact address' task row and its status, the '5. Consignment parties' row hint and the Review and submit control; (2) the contact address page at /consignment/contact/select (h1 'Contact address for consignment'), always reachable from the Overview, whose variants are first visit (nothing checked, no current-contact card) and return after a save (saved radio checked plus a 'Current contact address' summary card), and whose 'Add a new address' link renders only outside stub mode; (3) Review your notification at /notification-view, reached only by 5c7f8 after a full journey walk, mined for '5. Consignment parties' (the Roles and addresses card, six rows) and '6. Contact address', plus the transporter card the test does not check. Every contact-address test reaches the page by the same beforeEach walk (new notification, origin, commodity). The all-operators walk passes through the addresses hub, the five role pickers, CPH, arrival, transit, transporter and contact pages; those pages belong to other parts and are recorded here only as the route. Network logs hold only browser-to-frontend traffic: the address-book read behind the radio list is server-side and never seen. No trace recorded a browser error. What is conditional: the current-contact card (only once a contact is saved), the checked radio (only once saved), the Add a new address link (only outside stub mode), and the Overview task status (To do until a contact is saved, then Complete). This run re-mined the slice and re-checked the earlier extract's claims for it against the traces, keeping their ids where they still hold.
Part 8, Copied addresses: copy semantics, editing and freeze after submit (animals and address book): Part 8, copied addresses (animals journey and the INS address book behind it). Read in full: the three spec files addresses-copied.spec.ts (4 tests), addresses-edit.spec.ts (6 tests) and addresses-submit-freeze.spec.ts (2 tests) under repos/trade-imports-ins-tests/tests/animals/e2e/features/address-book/, and all 12 trace zips the partition names, every one passed. tim distil trace 'open' refused the traces (TraceVersionError: recorded by a newer Playwright), so, as the partition structure directs, each zip was read already unzipped in the part folder (trace-e2e.work/part8/<hash>/): every browser action from the N-trace.trace files (before events: goto, click, fill, check, selectOption, reload, expect), the rendered <main> of every frame snapshot (rendered to <hash>.main.html), the address book API calls and bodies in N-trace.network and resources/, and the test steps in test.trace. Refs below name the trace by its folder hash (b00d3, 0db17, 8eb85, 7de00 from addresses-copied; 923fb, e4503, 435a1, ecf01, bb8eb, 5c999 from addresses-edit; 4d3c6, db5da from addresses-submit-freeze) and the browser call id. Pages reached, in journey order: dashboard (/live-animals) and start of a notification (b00d3, 0db17 only, unseeded); Overview task list; Consignment addresses hub (/addresses, caption 'Consignment parties'), one summary-list row per role (Place of origin, Consignor or exporter, Consignee, Importer, Place of destination, County parish holding (CPH) number) with Add, or Change plus Edit details; the role picker (/consignors/select, /place-of-origin/select; heading = role name, search, a 5-per-page table of book records, pagination, 'Selected address:' inset); the edit-address form (/<role>/edit?return=addresses|notification-view, /consignment/contact/edit?return=consignment%2Fcontact%2Fselect; caption = role, heading 'Edit address details'); Contact address for consignment (/consignment/contact/select: radios of every book record plus a 'Current contact address' card); Review your notification (/notification-view) in Draft, Submitted and Amending states, incl. its error summary and per-row error; Declaration; Import notification submitted confirmation; dashboard search and Amend notification; Overview in Amending; Cancel this amendment? (/cancel-amend); review after cancelling (?cancelled=1 with a success banner). Conditional surface: Edit details only for a role holding a copy; Add only for an unanswered role; review error summary only when a copy breaks the rules or a section is incomplete; Change/Edit links and Continue absent on a submitted notification. Seeded tests (createDraftNotification) built the draft over HTTP form posts in a separate request context; only the UI part is browser-walked. Not reached: the contact edit form's error state, any validation other than name, postcode length, email format and country, a no-results picker search page render, editing a copy during an amendment, and what reaches the backend (server-side calls are not in a browser trace).
Part 9, Address picker, read-only roles and the INS add handshake (animals and address book): Part 9 mined all 15 trace zips its read names, from four spec files in the tests repo's animals project (tests/animals/e2e/features/address-book/), all of which were read in full: address-book-navigation.spec.ts (1: follows the Address book item from the animals journey to the INS address book and back [c4eb9]); addresses-add-handshake.spec.ts (2: saving a new address in INS returns to the picker with it selected and committed [bcd17]; cancelling INS add returns to the picker without saving an address [55254]); addresses-picker.spec.ts (1: the picker searches and pages the address book, and the row selected on a later page is the one that saves [98845]); addresses-read-only.spec.ts (11: per role, Consignor or exporter, Place of origin, Consignee, Importer, Place of destination, 'links to INS to add an address when the full stack is running' [6173e, feeb7, 8b5e4, fd6b1, 8ab82, all passed] and 'offers no INS add link in stub mode' [9a7a6, 20282, 0200a, 1bc3e, c3c13, all skipped after their beforeEach ran]; plus 'the create-address page is no longer served' [9baa5]). The bundled trace viewer refused every zip (TraceVersionError: the traces were recorded by a newer Playwright), so each zip was read from its unzipped copy in this part's work folder with jq: test.trace (test steps, locators and assertions), N-trace.trace (frame snapshots rendered back to HTML) and N-trace.network (resource snapshots, with request and response bodies under resources/). Refs name the trace by its folder hash fragment, then the call id of the snapshot or the request URL. The corpus ran against the compose stack (animals frontend on :3000, INS frontend on :3002, Defra ID stub on :3007, address-book API on :8089), not stub mode, which is why the five stub-mode tests skipped and their traces still show the INS add link. Pages in this slice, in the order a user meets them: (1) the Consignment addresses hub at /live-animals/notifications/{ref}/addresses, mined only for each role row's Add, Change and Edit details links and the value it shows before and after a pick; (2) the address picker, one per role, at /consignors/select, /place-of-origin/select, /consignees/select, /importers/select and /destinations/select: journey strip, caption Consignment parties, the role as h1, a one-line description, an Add a new address link to INS, a Search field with hint, a table of address-book rows each with a small radio and a View details disclosure, a 'Showing 5 of N addresses' caption, GOV.UK pagination at five rows a page, an inset showing the carried selection, and Save and continue; its variants are unfiltered page 1, page 2, searched to one row, searched to two rows, cleared, returned from INS with ?selected=, and re-entered after a save; (3) the Defra ID stub sign-in (Sign in using Government Gateway), met when the journey first crosses to INS; (4) the INS Add address details page at :3002/address-book/add with the handshake query, its fields and its two buttons, saved and cancelled; (5) the animals return endpoint /address-return, seen only as a redirect; (6) the create-address URL /addresses/create?for=consignor, which answers 404 Page not found; (7) the service navigation on both frontends, the INS Address book list at /address-book and the INS Dashboard at /, reached from the Address book item and left by the INS dashboard's Start a new notification link back to /live-animals. Snapshots of the picker itself are missing from two skipped traces (Consignor or exporter 9a7a6 and Place of destination c3c13): their network logs show the picker GET, but the trace closed before a snapshot. Through the API, creating a notification with an empty fulfilments list returns a DRAFT notification with a backend-minted GBN-AG reference number, concurrency token 0 and every content section null.

The backend notification entity carries id, referenceNumber, concurrencyToken, status, created, updated, submittedAt, a notification object (origin, commodity, reasonForImport, additionalDetails, placeOfOrigin, consignor, consignee, importer, destination, consignment, cphNumber, transport, purposeInInternalMarket, destinationCountry, portOfExit, exitDate) and fulfilments.
The fulfilment view (GET /notifications/{ref}/fulfilments) returns a reduced projection: referenceNumber, status, concurrencyToken, created, submittedAt and fulfilments.
POST /notifications/{ref}/submit moves a notification from DRAFT to SUBMITTED, increments its concurrency token and stamps submittedAt.
The backend accepts a submit for a notification whose content sections are all null; the API submit does not check completeness.
claims.note: Inferred from a 200 SUBMITTED response to an empty notification. Completeness gating, if any, sits in the frontend.

claims.statement: The fulfilment view reflects each transition: after submit it reports SUBMITTED with submittedAt set; after amend it reports AMEND.

claims.statement: POST /notifications/{ref}/cancel-amend returns an AMEND notification to SUBMITTED and increments the concurrency token.
Copy takes the source's current concurrency token as a query parameter (POST /notifications/{ref}/copy?concurrencyToken=N) and returns a new DRAFT notification with a new reference number.
Copy no longer de-duplicates: two copies of the same source with the same token produce two distinct DRAFT notifications.
Copying does not change the source notification, so a second copy can reuse the same concurrency token.
claims.quote: copy does not mutate the source, so both calls carry the same token.

claims.statement: A copy of a notification whose content was empty is itself empty; the trace does not show whether a copy of a filled notification carries its answers.
claims.note: The spec calls copy a WYSIWYG operation post-EUDPA-314, but no trace in this part copies a filled notification or walks the Copy as new button in the UI.

claims.statement: POST /notifications/{ref}/soft-delete sets the status to DELETED and increments the concurrency token, keeping the record.
Soft delete is idempotent: a repeat call returns the same DELETED notification without incrementing the concurrency token.
A SUBMITTED notification can be soft-deleted through the API (the deleted notification had already been submitted).
No trace in this part walks the Delete page (/delete) in the UI or shows how a soft-deleted notification appears, or stops appearing, on the dashboard.
No trace in this part shows the fulfilment view after cancel-amend, copy or soft delete, or a fulfilments list that is not empty.
No trace in this part shows what happens when a stale concurrency token is posted (a conflicting edit).
Every write from the journey forms carries a hidden concurrencyToken that increases by one with each saved change; the party select pages post it empty.

The address book API is scoped by organisation in its path: POST /organisation/{organisationId}/addresses creates an address (201, Location /organisation/{organisationId}/addresses/{id}), sent with an x-api-key header and a Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header.
claims.note: x-api-key value [REDACTED]. The call is made by the test fixture directly; the INS frontend's own calls to this API are server-side and not in the trace.

claims.statement: GET /organisation/{organisationId}/addresses/{id} returns one address, including a tombstoned one.
A stored address (the Standard Address Block) holds id, name, addressLine1, addressLine2, townOrCity, county, postcode, countryCode, phone, email, organisationId, deleted, createdAt and modifiedAt.

Addresses created through the API under organisation id 5900001 appear in the INS address book of users signed in to Gatwick Airport (SBI 110100101), so INS maps the signed-in organisation to address-book organisation 5900001.
claims.ref: trace 83967 request POST /organisation/5900001/addresses; trace f92fd action call@78; trace 3c6f9 action call@62
claims.note: How the SBI chosen at sign-in becomes organisation id 5900001 is not visible in the trace.

claims.statement: The INS frontend's own calls to the address book API (list, create, update, delete) happen server-side and none appears in the browser trace.

claims.statement: INS keeps one aggregated read-model document per notification in the trade-imports-ins-backend notifications collection, with the id Imports.Notification.GBN-AG.<reference number>.
claims.note: Asserted against Mongo by the spec; the test passed in trace 28659.

claims.statement: The aggregated document exists as soon as the notification is created (a NOTIFICATION_CREATED event fires at creation, before transport details are filled in), with status DRAFT.
claims.quote: NOTIFICATION_CREATED fires immediately at creation (before transport details are filled in), so we poll for the specific fully-populated state rather than bare status=DRAFT.

claims.statement: Before submission the aggregated document reflects the edited draft: status DRAFT, the reference number, origin country, commodity Cow, an arrival date in the future, a lastUpdated date and an aggregateVersion above 0.
claims.note: The journey posted countryOfOrigin=FR and arrivalDateAtPort=7/11/2026 (trace 28659), so originCountry is the country code.

claims.statement: The aggregated document's commodity is the common name Cow, resolved from the Bos taurus species the user picked.
Submitting updates the same aggregated document to SUBMITTED rather than creating a second one: exactly one document exists for the notification.
claims.quote: Then — same document is updated to SUBMITTED (no duplicate created) ... expect(await collection.countDocuments({ _id: aggregateId })).toBe(1);

claims.statement: After submission the aggregated document keeps the reference, origin country, commodity, future arrival date and a lastUpdated date, and its aggregateVersion is higher than the draft's.
The aggregated store is updated asynchronously from journey events: it catches up with the journey some time after each change rather than in the same request.
claims.quote: await expect.poll(() => collection.findOne({ _id: aggregateId, status: 'SUBMITTED' }), { timeout: timeouts.long }).not.toBeNull();
claims.note: The spec has to poll with a long timeout, and the INS dashboard still showed DRAFT for three searches after submission (claim trace-e2e-p15-106).

Each INS dashboard row has a View link that opens the notification in the frontend of the journey that owns it, as an absolute URL into that frontend (here the live-animals frontend).
